papers.title: KernelArmor: End-to-End Agentic System for Establishing Memory and Thread Safety for CUDA
papers.summary: Optimized CUDA kernels can pass testing while retaining subtle memory and concurrency bugs. We present KernelArmor, an agentic framework that combines LLM-generated annotations with an extended SMT verifier to establish memory and thread safety under explicit contracts. KernelArmor can reason about kernels with advanced CUDA features, such as tensor cores, packed accesses, warp synchronization, asynchronous copies, and library calls, returning source-level diagnostics to guide verification and repair. Across 740 instances containing 1,370 production-grade CUDA kernels, it reports potential bugs in 78.6% of instances and establishes safety for 11.4%, outperforming the evaluated state-of-the-art tools in detection coverage, identifying 100% of cuCatch memory-safety bugs and all in-scope cuHadron races. Integrated into an agentic optimization loop, KernelArmor produces verified kernels in all 77 trajectories while retaining 99% of the unconstrained geometric-mean speedup.

papers.title: Exstill: The Most Efficient Single-Chip Processor for the Next Token
papers.summary: Generating a token with a language model requires a fixed amount of arithmetic, whose energy sets a floor beneath any hardware. For Qwen3-1.7B at a 16K-token context, gate-level measurements at 5 nm place this floor at 0.89 mJ per token, yet an NVIDIA B300 spends 391-1,120x that. The excess is the price of generality, software layers, programmable hardware and moving weights and key-value (KV) caches from external memory, and it widens with each process generation. We present a co-design approach that brings token generation close to this floor and then lowers the floor itself, optimizing silicon and model together in a gate-level search loop. Fixing one model architecture in the datapath, with weights still loadable, and holding weights and every conversation's KV cache on-die, a pre-silicon 5 nm design brings an unchanged Qwen3-1.7B token to 3.4x its floor. Co-designing the model with the circuits at fixed quality lowers the floor to 0.29 mJ and the token to 0.52 mJ, 1.8x the new floor and less than the baseline model's arithmetic alone, while on-die capacity grows from one user to twelve. Against a measured B300 serving the same twelve users, the design decodes each user's tokens 110x faster at 690x lower energy. To show that one fixed architecture can serve, as a co-processor, the latency-critical workloads around a frontier model, we introduce Polyglot-DC (1.7B and 4B, each with its own design), specialized for each job by distillation and task-specific training into its own weights. As a drafter it speeds single-user speculative decoding of large open models by up to 6.6x at the maximum reasoning effort. Its guard returns multilingual verdicts in a millisecond or less, within a point of the strongest open guard. Its agent and financial-reasoning models lead comparable open models on established benchmarks, with a reasoning turn falling from seconds to tens of milliseconds.

papers.title: Lasso: Towards Sustainable AI-Generated Media Detection with Intel QAT On-Chip Compression
papers.summary: Synthetic text, images, and video are rising. Software-only detectors are power-hungry, too slow, and costly, and do not scale with demand. When software cannot scale, historically hardware often comes to the rescue. We perform the first reverse engineering of a compression accelerator--Intel QuickAssist Technology (QAT) microarchitecture and--find different amount of time on each, a novel data structure-dependent property. Using this information, we then build Lasso, a low-cost, high-performance detector for AI-generated content that turns the accelerator into a measuring instrument. For text detection, Lasso achieves 100% accuracy on original DetectRL text and retains 92% average accuracy after paraphrasing, compared with 78% for Binoculars and 55% for DetectGPT. Across original, paraphrased, and perturbed text, it achieves 82% average accuracy, outperforming all five baselines. With topic, length, and formatting matched, accuracy reaches 95% for instruction-tuned generators, including when the tested generator is unseen. On RAID, accuracy averages 82% when trained on one generator and tested on another, and 74% across eight held-out domains. Detection takes 0.74 microseconds, a speedup of at least 83,784x across five baselines. At the same time, Lasso consumes over 99% less energy per document than both Binoculars and DetectGPT. At the same time, Lasso detects AI-generated videos, software code, and images with 67.5%, 70% and 78% accuracy, respectively, with low latency and power opening avenues for practical real time and edge device detection of multimodality AI artifacts for the first time. No other compared technique supports detection across all four modalities: text, video, images, and code.

papers.title: Coordinating Distributed AI Servers with Industrial Loads to Reduce Grid-Interconnection Needs
papers.summary: We show that co-locating distributed AI servers with industrial demand and coordinating AI workloads with production loads can substantially reduce the additional grid interconnection that AI computing requires. Grid interconnection is increasingly constraining the expansion of large AI data centers. Factories already have grid connections sized for their peak production loads, and we propose hosting AI servers during production valleys. We formulate a joint optimization that sizes CPU and GPU servers, schedules deadline-constrained tasks, and routes tasks among factories, and use it to compare three factory-site architectures with new large data centers serving the same demand. Applying this framework to 31 Chinese manufacturing industries, we find that AI demand and production loads often do not peak together. As a result, AI servers placed at factories and scheduled according to production peaks need about 60% less additional interconnection capacity than new large data centers, and 98% less when tasks are routed among a group's factories.

papers.title: Supercharging Olmo-core for Efficient and Scalable MoE Training
papers.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models add parameters without proportionally increasing per-token compute. However, training cost also depends on bytes moved, memory held, and kernels launched, and many of those costs follow total parameter size rather than active compute. On infrastructure built for dense models, this mismatch is costly: in early baselines, throughput fell as stored expert parameter size grew, even though the useful work per token stayed nearly fixed. To close this gap, we present a redesigned training stack in Olmo-core, built for efficient, scalable MoE training. We replace the Fully Sharded Data Parallel (FSDP) of earlier Olmo-core versions with an architecture built on Distributed Data Parallel (DDP), and add Expert Parallelism (EP), Pipeline Parallelism (PP), a distributed optimizer, and activation recompute. We propose NVSHMEM-based rowwise EP, which writes each token directly into its expert's buffer, avoiding dispatch and combine permutation overhead. We make EP fully synchronization-free by keeping routing metadata on the GPU and using device-scheduled grouped GEMMs. Closely integrated MXFP8 cuts compute, activation-memory, and transport costs, and topology-agnostic checkpoints let the parallel layout change between runs. On NVL8 B300 nodes, the stack supports training configurations from 12.9 billion to 1.2 trillion total parameters on up to 512 GPUs, reaching 858 useful-model TFLOP/s/GPU at 1.2 trillion with MXFP8 and per-layer recompute; an experimental capacity test with the optional DeepEP v2 backend reaches 2.38 trillion. We also explain each design choice and share findings for other training systems; for example, we identify a failure pattern we call Token Gerrymandering, in which the MoE router can learn to hack the load-balancing loss, and find that overlapping communication with computation can slow the overlapped kernels by more than it hides.

papers.title: NVFP4-MLA: Unified FP4 KV-Cache Storage and Attention Computation for Multi-Head Latent Attention
papers.summary: Long-context reasoning and agentic workloads make key-value (KV) cache capacity and attention computation the dominant costs of serving frontier large language models. We present NVFP4-MLA, the first design to push both KV-cache storage and attention computation of multi-head latent attention (MLA) to FP4. NVFP4-MLA co-designs the quantization algorithm with the attention kernel and the cache system. Selective residual compensation preserves model accuracy by adding NVFP4 residuals only to the quantization-sensitive channels. Two-dimensional quantization blocks make the shared latent cache compatible with the different reduction directions of the two attention batched matrix multiplications (BMMs), removing requantization between them. On DeepSeek-R1 and Kimi-K3, NVFP4-MLA matches BF16 MLA average accuracy across nine benchmarks while compressing the MLA KV cache by 3.20x and 3.05x relative to BF16 MLA. On NVIDIA Rubin GPUs, NVFP4-MLA speeds up the attention kernel over FP8 MLA by up to 2.82x on DeepSeek-R1 and 2.71x on Kimi-K3, and lowers p90 time to first token in agentic multi-turn serving by up to 3.5x and 2.1x, respectively. In disaggregated DeepSeek-R1 serving, it also raises per-GPU throughput by up to 2.30x.

papers.title: NEMESIS2.0: LLM-Aided Netlist-Driven Performance Equation Modeling for Accelerated Analog Circuit Sizing
papers.summary: This work presents NEMESIS2.0, an open-source LLM-aided framework that automatically derives equation-based performance models for analog circuits. The resulting equations provide fast, accurate surrogates for SPICE evaluation. To validate the method, equation-based models are developed for seven circuit test cases in a commercial 65nm CMOS technology, covering 15 metrics on five operational transconductance amplifier topologies, and six metrics on two dynamic comparator topologies. When tested on 1000 unseen variants of these seven designs, each corresponding to a different set of independently sampled transistor sizes, the accuracy is found to be within 5% of SPICE. To demonstrate use cases for NEMESIS2.0, the generated models are used as performance evaluators in multiple transistor sizers based on different population-based stochastic search optimizers. For each of the seven test cases, transistor sizing is performed for 100 different sets of performance specifications, with final SPICE simulation confirming that 83.3% of the resulting designs meet all specifications after a single sizing run. The rest fail to meet the specifications due to discrepancies between the model and SPICE, and require iterative resizing under tightened specifications; all such scenarios meet specifications within five iterations. Within the transistor sizers, this equation-based performance analysis evaluates ~400 design candidates per second, versus 0.14 candidates per second for SPICE-based evaluation, achieving 196-238x sizing runtime speedup, including final SPICE verification.

papers.title: RF-Based Macronutrient Estimation in Liquid Foods via Composition-Aware Multi-Task Learning
papers.summary: Current approaches to macronutrient estimation range from high-overhead laboratory analysis to user-dependent methods such as manual nutritional lookup, reading package labels, and vision-based image analysis. These approaches are often time-consuming, input-dependent, or sensitive to imaging and measurement conditions. In this work, we investigate synchronous 2.4 GHz OFDM radio-frequency (RF) measurements for estimating carbohydrate, fat, and protein content in liquid foods. Using a controlled sensing setup, we study how liquid composition shapes frequency-domain RF responses -- a first step toward a sensor integrated into a liquid-contacting vessel that estimates macronutrient content passively and label-free, and toward composition-aware RF food analysis beyond liquids. We propose the Ingredient-Conditioned OFDM Transformer (ICOT), a structure-aware multi-task Transformer that operates on two-dimensional OFDM channel frequency response matrices. ICOT infers canonical ingredient categories representing dielectric-driver composition and uses them to condition macronutrient regression through feature concatenation. On 28,420 captures spanning 55 beverage classes, ICOT achieves an in-distribution MAE of 0.101 g/100 ml and an out-of-distribution MAE of 0.485 g/100 ml -- comparable in magnitude to deviations present in manufacturer-reported labels -- though generalization to novel formulations remains the primary open challenge.

papers.title: Run, Read Back, Refine: Observation Fidelity in Execution-Grounded EDA Agents
papers.summary: Design engineers lose the most time orchestrating flows and patching the gaps where closed EDA tools refuse to interoperate. We present an execution-grounded LLM agent for PyAether, SKILL, and Tcl that closes a generate-execute-refine loop over unified MCP tools (API retrieval, documentation, sandbox execution) and is already deployed in production EDA flows, with a grounding-gap framework positing that EDA-scripting correctness is bottlenecked by observation fidelity at the L4 (situated) layer, which model scale alone cannot reach. On EDA-Scripting-Bench (449 tasks, three languages, four commercial runtimes), the system reaches 76.5% pooled Pass@1 versus 19.7% (pure LLM): the system-level observation axis spans 56.8 percentage points with the model fixed, exceeding the 23.3-percentage-point backbone range with the harness fixed---two axes answering different questions; observation is an under-invested axis whose returns are measurable and graded.

papers.title: Can Agentic LLMs Write Task-Based Parallel Code? A Study of OpenMP Tasking, HPX, StarPU and TTG
papers.summary: Task-based programming offers more expressive power than loop-level parallelism, but the runtimes providing it differ widely in API style, maturity, and the amount of public code to learn from. This paper asks how well LLM agents write C++ for four of them: OpenMP Tasking, HPX, StarPU, and TTG. Instead of single one-shot prompts, we use an agentic workflow in which the model edits files, compiles, and runs its kernels until it reproduces a reference output. Five locally hosted open-weight LLM implement seven HPC kernels, including matrix multiplication, Cholesky and LU factorization, in all four frameworks and a serial baseline to verify their understanding of the problem in general. Every kernel is evaluated independently for correctness at each concurrency level, strong scaling, and peak memory. Model capability dominates the outcome: three models produce correct, genuinely task-parallel kernels in 57-82% of the cases, while two models rarely compile their own code and almost never succeed. For the capable models, OpenMP Tasking and HPX are handled most reliably, StarPU is close behind, and TTG trails. The best generated GEMM and factorization kernels match or exceed the multithreaded OpenBLAS/LAPACK reference. However, correctness overstates parallel quality: several "parallel" kernels contain no parallelism at all; and serialized task graphs and unsuitable task granularity remain common.

papers.title: Decoupling Data Layouts from Algebraic Data Types
papers.summary: Algebraic data types (ADTs) decouple the logical structure of data from physical layout choices that affect performance. For example, packing small fields into a word improves spatial locality, while storing co-accessed fields contiguously can enable vectorization. Such choices reinforce or undermine one another, with ramifications for compiler optimizations and memory management. Their interplay creates a combinatorial space of layouts with different runtime costs and memory footprints. The most favorable layout depends on the program's construction and destruction patterns, the characteristics of input data, and the target machine. Exploring this space requires control over layout decisions and a way to compose them while preserving program semantics. We provide both through rewrite rules over layouts, independent of any particular source language or bit-level encoding. Starting from a canonical layout derived from the ADT, these rules transform its representation while leaving the source program intact. We identify a local refinement criterion for proving each rewrite rule correct, so that layouts continue to represent every value and keep distinct values apart. Adding a new rule therefore only requires a proof satisfying this local criterion. We realize these rules in Isomer, a new pure functional programming language whose compiler specializes construction, pattern matching, and memory management to the chosen layouts. Using a default layout for all ADTs, Isomer achieves competitive performance against established functional compilers that automatically select layouts. Our rewrites further improve performance by tailoring layouts to each workload, permitting representations that prior work cannot attain or can only achieve through explicit changes to the source code.

papers.title: A Nonlinear Abstract Domain for Bayesian Neural Networks
papers.summary: Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) explicitly model epistemic uncertainty by leveraging probability distributions over network parameters, making them better suited for risk-aware decision-making. Yet soundly propagating uncertainty through the network and capturing the entire output distribution to support predictive uncertainty quantification remains a fundamental challenge. Existing approaches are either sampling-based, providing no formal guarantees, or propagate only selected statistical properties, such as expectations and entropy, limiting their applicability to general probabilistic queries. To address these challenges, we present the first nonlinear abstract domain for soundly approximating complete probability distributions of BNNs. The abstract domain builds upon a novel marginal collecting concrete semantics that soundly abstracts the classical joint-measure semantics. It combines support partitioning with exponential-affine bounds to represent probability measures, capturing both discrete and continuous components of mixed distributions as well as nonlinear density shapes over bounded and unbounded supports. We develop sound abstract transformers that can efficiently handle high-dimensional affine transformations and nonlinear ReLU activations, while remaining highly parallelizable. We further extend the framework beyond BNNs to support bounded-loop probabilistic programs with Bayesian inference to demonstrate its generality. We implement the resulting abstract interpreter as a GPU-accelerated analyzer. Experimental results show that the framework significantly improves precision over existing probabilistic reasoning approaches while soundly capturing the complete output distribution, demonstrating strong efficiency and scalability.

papers.title: Budgeted Decision-Model-Guided Joint-Action Search for Satellite Edge Computing
papers.summary: Efficient task offloading in satellite edge computing requires coordinated allocation of communication and computing resources. Search methods based on large language models (LLMs) have been shown to generate high-quality resource allocations, but the latency of individual model requests and repeated model interactions can lead to substantial solver overhead. We propose budgeted joint-action search (BJAS), an integrated decision-model-guided solver that jointly optimizes satellite offloading and power allocation to minimize average task-completion latency under explicit search budgets. Its bounded candidate pools combine single-terminal updates with power-inheriting offload replacements for batched selection, retaining two-terminal coordination without enumerating additional power vectors. Across 60 completed runs per method under the workflows' respective configurations, BJAS reduces mean total solver time by 97.16% relative to LLM-generated offloading while achieving a mean task-completion latency close to that of the LLM baseline. BJAS also achieves lower mean task-completion latency than the tested genetic algorithm and deep deterministic policy gradient baselines.

papers.title: Feedback-Aware Residual Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Timely Communication in Cognitive Radio Networks
papers.summary: Supporting time-sensitive services in cognitive radio networks requires distributed access strategies that translate shared spectrum opportunities into timely packet delivery. Achieving this objective is challenging because reception conditions are only partially observable to individual transmitters, while dynamic competition and access overhead constrain the service that can be completed within packet deadlines. We formulate a distributed access problem that captures the coupling among interference-dependent reception, queue evolution, and protocol durations. To address this problem, we propose feedback-aware residual multi-agent proximal policy optimization (FAR-MAPPO) under centralized training and decentralized execution. The method constructs channel-specific historical feedback representations that complement instantaneous sensing with evidence from completed access attempts. A residual policy network integrates this experience with current observations and packet urgency to guide local access decisions. Numerical results show improved timely delivery over the baseline methods, particularly under heavy traffic and bursty arrivals with mixed packet deadlines.

papers.title: EdgeNet City: Context-Aware AI-RAN Planning toward Autonomous Urban Connectivity
papers.summary: The evolution from 5G toward 6G calls for more anticipatory and context-aware Cell-on-Wheels (COW) planning in wireless networks. We present EdgeNet City, an online framework that grounds free-form natural-language inputs in geographic activity representations and path-gain data. A catalog-referenced representation links activity roles, geographic features and predefined demand profiles, separating semantic selection from deterministic spatial computation. The algorithm combines prescribed demand with relative propagation support to screen service areas for subsequent COW assessment. We publicly release a London dataset with 22,678 transmitters, approximately 449.4 billion path-gain records and retained receiver geometry. Within prepared propagation domains, the online prototype reuses these records without new ray tracing or live operator measurements. In a matched 20-event study across six London environments, the expanded representation increases mean spatial overlap with the reused full technical-review reference from 0.4929 for the single-feature Venue-only baseline to 0.7203. Rule-based and language-model planners select identical activities in this panel. With need-aware ranking and a three-cell diagnostic budget fixed, the expanded representation increases mean Reference-need Capture by 25.44 percentage points over Venue-only.

papers.title: Rethinking KV Caching for LLM Decode: Free-Space Optical KV Regeneration for Reduction of Memory Traffic
papers.summary: Long-context large language model (LLM) decoding repeatedly reads the historical key-value (KV) cache, making multi-head attention (MHA) memory-bandwidth-bound. Caching layer-input activations instead halves historical-cache storage and traffic, but requires regenerating KV from each cached activation. On digital accelerators such as GPUs, this regeneration takes far longer than fetching the activation from HBM. The KV regeneration overhead outweighs the savings from reduced memory traffic, shifting decode attention from a memory bottleneck to a compute bottleneck. We present OptiDecode, a hybrid optoelectronic decode-attention accelerator that regenerates historical KV using free-space optics and computes attention digitally. Projection weights remain resident on optical tiles, exploiting reuse across historical tokens for high-throughput optical regeneration. Scaling to large models introduces two challenges. First, distributing weights across tiles requires sending the same activations to every head group, while each readout die produces only partial KV. Activation replay shares one set of electrical-to-optical converters across head groups without costly broadcast. In-situ attention avoids transferring partial KV from readout dies to reducers by computing on them locally and exchanging only partial scores, probabilities, and partial outputs. Second, processing an activation chunk through all dependent stages takes longer than one activation-fetch interval. Chunk pipelining overlaps successive chunks so that OptiDecode sustains the HBM activation-fetch rate. OptiDecode demonstrates 1.92-1.99x decode-attention speedup over an ideal GPU KV-read baseline at equal peak HBM bandwidth (A100-B200), for 32K-token contexts across evaluated 30B-175B MHA models, approaching the 2x upper bound from halving historical memory traffic.

papers.title: SliceWise: Traffic-Aware Multi-Agent RL with Temporal Encoding for Joint Slice Admission and Resource Orchestration in O-RAN
papers.summary: Ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) services in mission-critical applications such as industrial automation, remote healthcare, and autonomous systems demand stringent quality-of-service (QoS) guarantees under dynamic, resource-constrained wireless conditions. Open radio access networks (O-RAN) offer a software-defined and programmable foundation for embedding AI-driven control. This letter proposes SliceWise, a traffic-aware multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MARL) framework for joint admission control, user-slice association, and resource orchestration in O-RAN. The control problem is modeled as a cooperative multi-agent Markov decision process, with long short-term memory (LSTM) networks capturing temporal traffic dynamics and dueling double deep Q-networks (D3QN) ensuring stable learning. Simulation results show that SliceWise substantially reduces delay violations and packet drops while improving slice-level reliability and resource efficiency, offering a scalable orchestration solution for AI-native O-RAN deployments.

papers.title: Predicting, Fast and Slow: SSD Already Knows Which Guess Is Wrong
papers.summary: Heimdall, a learned controller, calls slow on 52% of an SSD's reads when 30% are slow. Uncertainty estimators, the remedy prescribed for its wrong guesses, cannot find them: nine of them do no better than a coin. The drive can. On one trace, 2% of the reads of 4 to 8 KiB that found less than 4 KiB outstanding while the drive was answering came back slow, and Heimdall called 96% of them slow. A 4,096-entry table of how the drive's recent reads came back, untrained and 21 ns a decision, ranks the wrong guesses at a median AUROC of 0.68 on 57 held-out traces, where the nine sit at 0.46 to 0.52, and it predicts slow reads better than Heimdall itself.

papers.title: Sustaining In-Network Computation in Satellite Networks: An Architecture for Semantic Continuity
papers.summary: Satellite computations often outlast the paths and providers initially serving them. We argue that in-network computing should organize changing execution opportunities around one continuing logical computation: workers execute ready operations, while consumers recognize which results already contribute. We present an architecture separating logical computation, stream context, and physical binding, and show in wildfire assessment how retained observations support recomputation while reachable association history stays in place. A 300-node Linux prototype examines placement, dependency assembly, and continuation. Across 120 images, stage-wise placement delivers 82.08% of positions within deadlines versus 76.06% for single-node placement, while traces separate blocked output delivery from dependencies split across providers. Across 50 observations with 20-node isolation, Confirmation-Coordinated Rebinding (CCR) coordinates replanning, source replay, cross-attempt acceptance, and in-band confirmation to complete all 50 observations with verified outputs using seven replays and 13 ignored duplicate outputs.

papers.title: Formalizing $\mathsf{einsum}$ with Named Tensor Notation
papers.summary: Einstein notation ($\mathsf{einsum}$) is a widely adopted tensor operation that has proven useful in areas such as machine learning and quantum computing. But it had no formal semantics until recently, and its properties had no mechanized verification. We formalize the denotational semantics of a language of tensors (multi-dimensional arrays) that supports $\mathsf{einsum}$ and repeated tensors ($\mathsf{expand}$). With this semantics, we verify equational rewriting rules about $\mathsf{einsum}$ and $\mathsf{expand}$ that improve the performance of tensor computation. Whereas typical languages use unnamed tensors, whose shape is a sequence of natural numbers, we found it advantageous for mechanization to use named tensors, whose shape is a finite map from names to natural numbers. To our knowledge, this is the first time that the semantics and rewriting rules of $\mathsf{einsum}$ are mechanized in a proof assistant. Our solution is agnostic to proof assistants; we have implemented it in Lean and partially in Agda.

papers.title: Compiling Imperative Hardware Protocol Specifications to Hardware
papers.summary: Correct modular composition in hardware depends on interfaces with subtle multi-cycle timing behavior, yet such protocols remain difficult to specify, test, and debug. Recent work has demonstrated that hardware communication specifications can take the form of compact imperative programs that describe the cycle-by-cycle behavior of each logical transaction. However, prior tools only use these specifications for simulation-based testing and debugging, and their semantics remain informal. In this work, we develop a theory of hardware protocol specifications using automata. In addition to making the specifications' meaning precise, the automaton representation lets us compile them into synthesizable hardware. We implement a compiler that produces RTL modules for driving hardware interfaces and for reconstructing logical transactions from low-level I/O signals. We demonstrate a variety of use cases for synthesizable protocol drivers and reconstructors, including runtime monitors that check security properties in the Wishbone protocol and a binding generator that synthesizes interfaces between RTL modules and programs in the Calyx intermediate language.

papers.title: DT-MATCH: Defect- and Topology-Aware Chiplet Matching for Yield Optimization in Heterogeneous Integration
papers.summary: Heterogeneous integration (HI) and advanced packaging enable chiplet-based system-on-chip (SoC) designs; however, they also introduce new yield challenges arising from manufacturing defects and complex die-to-die (D2D) interconnect constraints. In particular, lane-level defects, limited spares, and strict structural compatibility requirements impede the efficient assembly of functional systems from defective but repairable chiplets. We present DT-MATCH, a defect- and topology-aware chiplet matching framework that maximizes the number of functional SoCs under realistic assembly constraints. DT-MATCH provides two complementary approaches. The integer linear programming (ILP)-based approach is implemented using a batching strategy to approximate the exact formulation. The greedy randomized adaptive search procedure (GRASP)-based approach provides substantial acceleration, but it does not guarantee yield optimality. Both approaches use a preprocessing pipeline to reduce the problem size. Experimental results on industrial designs demonstrate that, as expected, the ILP-based approach achieves superior solution quality. The GRASP-based approach leads to lower runtimes while still achieving solution quality that is comparable to the ILP-based solution. Together, these methods provide a trade-off between solution quality and efficiency for practical chiplet assembly optimization.

papers.title: Diagnosis as Percolation on an Evidence Graph: Root-Cause Recoverability in Network Fault Diagnosis
papers.summary: Diagnosing failures from incomplete observations presents three challenges: determining whether sufficient evidence connects a possible cause to a symptom, distinguishing the true cause from plausible alternatives, and assessing when a diagnosis can be trusted. We introduce an evidence-graph framework that separates these challenges and uses percolation theory to analyze how missing information affects cause-symptom connectivity. In controlled simulations with an average degree of four, a giant connected component emerges when approximately 25% of evidence is retained, but a specific cause-alarm pair reaches 50% connectivity only after slightly more than half is retained. Even connectivity does not guarantee correct cause identification. We apply this framework to multi-LLM diagnosis of IEEE 802.11 packet captures. A final reconciliation pass improves evidence-grounding weighted F1 from 0.912 to 0.964, primarily by removing isolated citations rather than connecting previously separate evidence chains, consistently across three graph constructions. However, connectivity is not a reliable confidence measure: its association with diagnostic quality becomes statistically insignificant after controlling for capture length, citation count, within-capture dependence, and multiple comparisons. Further experiments show that directed and weighted edges help selectively, while simpler overlap measures or domain-specific methods sometimes perform better. These findings establish evidence graphs as a framework for separating evidence availability, causal distinguishability, and confidence reliability, while demonstrating that connected evidence alone cannot certify diagnostic correctness.

papers.title: IA-MoE: An Intensity-Aware Mixture of Experts for DNN Inference
papers.summary: With the ever-increasing parameter scale and structural complexity of deep neural network (DNN) models, traditional cloud-based inference encounters bottlenecks in performance, privacy protection, and energy efficiency. While edge computing and edge intelligence facilitate the migration of inference tasks to edge servers closer to the data source, existing end-edge-cloud collaborative inference still encounters critical challenges, such as sensitivity to heterogeneous resources, complexity in multi-objective optimization, and adaptability to dynamic workloads. To achieve the joint optimization of end-to-end latency and energy consumption under dynamic inference requests with multi-resource constraints, we propose IA-MoE, an intensity-aware Mixture of Experts (MoE) framework. By modeling the model partitioning problem as a bilateral matching problem between layer tasks and virtual machine resources for each inference request, IA-MoE dynamically partitions DNN models in an edge-cloud hybrid computing environment. We evaluate IA-MoE using three representative DNNs (i.e., AlexNet, VGG16, ResNet50) on two public inference datasets in an enhanced CloudSimSDN simulation environment. Experimental results demonstrate that IA-MoE outperforms baseline methods regarding weighted normalized metrics for end-to-end latency and energy consumption. To our knowledge, this is the first study to introduce the MoE paradigm for DNN partitioning and collaborative inference in hybrid computing environments, providing a practical solution for efficient inference in artificial intelligence applications.

papers.title: MIAO: Microscaling Intermediate Accumulation Optimization
papers.summary: Microscaling (MX) quantization enables lower-precision large language model (LLM) inference with limited accuracy degradation, reducing memory requirement and multiplication cost. However, despite reduced operand precision, accumulation is often retained at high floating-point precisions, leaving a substantial hardware cost that operand quantization alone does not address. In particular, systolic arrays, as used in tensor accelerators such as Google TPU and AWS Trainium, distribute accumulation across distinct processing elements but conventionally use uniform accumulator precision throughout the array. This spatial organization offers an opportunity to reduce hardware cost by tailoring precision to individual accumulation stages. In this work, we present MIAO, a hardware-software co-design framework that jointly selects product precision and stage-dependent accumulator widths to minimize hardware area and energy cost under an end-to-end perplexity constraint. MIAO first calibrates MX block-scale shifts to reduce intermediate magnitudes while preserving operand quantization accuracy, then assigns narrower accumulators to earlier stages and progressively wider accumulators to later stages. To efficiently explore the resulting design space, MIAO combines hardware cost estimates derived from logic synthesis with a calibrated accuracy predictor to identify promising precision configurations, then validates the accuracy of promising candidates through bit-exact end-to-end LLM evaluation. Across MXFP8, MXFP6, and MXFP4, MIAO reduces processing element (PE) array area by up to 38.7% and energy by up to 36.1% relative to the all-BF16 accumulation baseline, with at most 1.60% additional perplexity degradation over operand-only MX quantization across six LLMs.

papers.title: HBF-EventLab: A Discrete-Event Simulator for Studying Host-Device Coordination in High Bandwidth Flash
papers.summary: High Bandwidth Flash (HBF) combines NAND flash density with high-bandwidth accelerator connectivity, offering additional memory capacity for large language model inference. However, limited hardware availability makes it difficult to evaluate how host behavior and device resource constraints jointly affect HBF request processing. We present HBF-EventLab, an open-source, transaction-level discrete-event simulator based on the Open Compute Project HBF specification. HBF-EventLab connects host request dispatch, command admission, fragmented write assembly, read dispatch, NAND execution, and completion feedback within a shared event loop. It explicitly models distinct resource lifetimes and separates configurable scheduling policies from ordering and resource constraints, enabling controlled exploration of host-device coordination. Experiments show how resource limits, address interleaving, fragment arrival patterns, and scheduling policies affect write completion and request latency. The results highlight the need to consider resource limits and scheduling policies jointly, accounting for their interactions with write assembly and read eligibility. We also integrate HBF-EventLab with real GPU execution of Qwen3-0.6B, combining profiled GPU activity durations with simulated weight-access delays to estimate time to first token and time per output token, with logits and output tokens remaining bitwise identical to those from native GPU execution. HBF-EventLab provides a configurable foundation for studying HBF mechanisms, exploring scheduling policies, and assessing how HBF access delays affect application-level timing. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/sjtu-epcc/HBF-EventLab.

papers.title: Restoring Fair Hrtick Re-arming After Same-Task Repicks in the Linux EEVDF Scheduler
papers.summary: Linux uses one-shot high-resolution scheduler ticks (hrticks) to request rescheduling at fair-class execution boundaries. We analyze a gap in the dispatch path in which an expired fair hrtick is not restarted when the fair scheduler selects the current task again. The gap arises because the same-task fast path bypasses set_next_task_fair(), the location that normally records the next fair hrtick delay. We introduce SNT_REPICK, an explicit same-task activation type for struct sched_class. For fair tasks, it preserves the fast path while restarting the hrtick from refreshed EEVDF state. For SCHED_DEADLINE, it deliberately performs no hrtick restart because the corresponding runtime state is not refreshed on a repick. The implementation was merged into the mainline Linux kernel as commit c72945693b. We give a conditional timing analysis for systems on which the periodic scheduler tick remains active and report validation from two platforms. Functional tests on an 80-core Ampere Altra exercised fair hrtick, deadline hrtick, and the CONFIG_HIGH_RES_TIMERS=n fallback. Independently, Intel's 0-Day Kernel Test Service reported a 34.2% increase in its stress-ng.rawudp.packets_32_bytes_received_per_sec metric on a 192-thread Intel Xeon 6740E under the documented test configuration. We distinguish this reported benchmark result from causal claims that require separate scheduler and network instrumentation.

papers.title: Exhaustive Evaluation of Fixed-Point Reciprocal Architectures for FPGAs
papers.summary: Fixed-point reciprocals are used in normalization and division on field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). Designs that share an output format can differ in worst-case error and in their need for memory and multipliers. The effect of table width, internal precision and refinement was evaluated for reciprocal computation in the Q16.16 and Q8.24 formats. Every representable input in the interval from 0.5 to 2.5 was tested against an exact integer reference. Five arithmetic paths were reconstructed from register-transfer-level source. Guarded interpolation, Newton-Raphson refinement and residual correction were then evaluated alongside polynomial and digit-recurrence baselines. Correct rounding was verified for all 131,073 Q16.16 and 33,554,433 Q8.24 inputs by adding one residual check to a guarded interpolated seed and one refinement step. An implementation with product reuse was verified at one input per cycle with a latency of 10 cycles in both formats. The Q8.24 implementation used nine digital signal processing slices in 7 series synthesis. The exact radix-2 control used no such slices and had a latency of 28 cycles. The reconstructed refined paths reduced the maximum relative error by factors of 205 to 223 when eight fractional bits were added. The evaluated designs provide reproducible choices for fixed accuracy budgets. In particular, correct rounding can be obtained on the tested interval by using a compact seed and checking the integer residual before the result is returned.

papers.title: Two-Robot Evacuation from a Unit Disk in the Segment Visibility Model
papers.summary: Under segment visibility, two robots discover a target as soon as it belongs to the segment joining their positions, even if neither robot has physically reached it. We study two unit-speed robots starting at the center of a unit disk that must both reach an exit (target) placed at an unknown point of its boundary. In our model robots are permitted to leave the disk while searching. We give a three-phase tangent-and-arc algorithm whose exact worst-case evacuation time is 2\sqrt{3}+\pi/3 \approx 4.511299$. We also prove a matching lower bound for the class of descending horizontal full-slice sweeps, allowing asymmetric robot trajectories. The proof uses an exterior path-length inequality and a feasible minimum-half-width symmetrization. Determining the optimal time over all segment-visibility algorithms remains open.

papers.title: CleanRoute: Reconciling DRC Compliance, Post-Layout Performance, and Runtime in Analog Routing
papers.summary: Automated analog routing remains a long-standing challenge because design-rule checking (DRC) compliance, post-layout performance preservation, and runtime reduction are difficult to achieve together. Existing analog routers have limited coverage of joined-metal design rules, lack control over topology-induced mismatch, and face a trade-off between DRC violations and runtime on uniform routing grids. In this paper, we introduce CleanRoute, an analog router that reconciles these three targets. Hierarchical rule enforcement assigns DRC checks and repairs to stages where the required geometry is complete, covering rules both between separate metal and where metal joins. IR-drop isolation constructs supply trees from current-mirror relationships and device currents to reduce topology-induced mismatch that geometric matching cannot eliminate and voltage drops along high-current paths. A flush-line grid adds net-specific lines aligned with device-metal edges to a coarse routing grid, providing DRC-compliant connections without uniform refinement. Experiments on ten operational transconductance amplifiers (OTAs) in a commercial 40nm process show that CleanRoute produces DRC-clean and functional layouts that pass layout versus schematic (LVS) checking on all benchmarks, with the strongest overall performance preservation and a median routing runtime of 8.82s, whereas the baselines produce no DRC-clean layouts.

papers.title: Making Preemption Productive in Long-Output LLM Serving
papers.summary: Reasoning LLMs generate long outputs whose key--value (KV) caches occupy GPU memory for minutes. When memory fills, the server preempts requests, and a preempted request can repeatedly lose and recover its state while producing little new output. We call this behavior KV thrashing. In certain cases, existing systems leave more than a fifth of requests stalled for over a minute. Because preemption cannot be avoided without delaying admission, we ask how to make it productive. We present Stint, a serving system that preserves a preempted request's work, bounds how long it waits, and gives it fresh output after it returns. Stint stores fixed-length KV snapshots in a contiguity-first CPU pool with an exact-extent allocator, and moves them with fused K/V gather/scatter kernels and double buffering. Age-based readmission brings stalled requests back, and protection gives them a turn of fresh decoding before another preemption. Remaining-length estimates from decoding hidden states guide victim selection. On olympiad-math replays with Qwen3-32B on H200 GPUs, no request pauses for more than 50 seconds under Stint and p99 time per output token falls by 50.7\% relative to recomputation in the same engine. The replay as a whole finishes 10.7\% sooner (12.0\% higher throughput), because the requests that baselines starve no longer finish last.

papers.title: IZM-DSR: A New Zone-Disjoint Multi-path Routing Algorithm for Mobile Ad-Hoc Network
papers.summary: Some of multi-path routing algorithms in MANETs use multiple paths simultaneously. These algorithms can attempt to find node-disjoint to achieve higher fault tolerance. By using node-disjoint paths, it is expected that the end-to-end delay in each case should be independent of each other. However, because of natural properties and medium access mechanisms in ad hoc networks, such as CSMA/CA, the endto-end delay between any source and destination depends on the pattern of communication in the neighborhood region. In this case some of the intermediate nodes should be silent to reverence their neighbors and this matter increases the end-toend delay. To avoid this problem, multi-path routing algorithms can use zone-disjoint paths instead of node-disjoint paths. In this paper we propose a new multi-path routing algorithm that selects zone-disjoint paths, using omnidirectional antenna. We evaluate our algorithm in several different scenarios. The simulation results show that our approach is very effective in decreasing routing overhead and end-to-end delay.

papers.title: TileCache: Serving Multi-Round Diffusion Image Editing with Compressed Activation Caches
papers.summary: Multi-round diffusion image editing can reduce computation by reusing intermediate activations, but retaining these activations across editing rounds introduces substantial memory and bandwidth overheads. Compression can reduce these overheads, but efficient cache construction is challenging: compressing only after editing requires buffering over 100 GB of activations per request. Moreover, the compressed cache must support selective reuse, as future masked edits require only a subset of the cached activations. It also exposes a scheduling challenge, as cached edits are faster than initial generations, causing naive policies to severely delay either initial generations or editing requests. In this paper, we aim to address both challenges through compression-informed serving. We develop TileCache, a serving system for multi-round diffusion editing. It compresses reusable activations and incorporates a scheduler that balances both edits and initial generation requests. Compared with the state-of-the-art image editing baseline, TileCache sustains over 2x the request arrival rate at 90% SLO attainment. It completes edits 2.4-4.5x and initial generations 1.3-2.2x faster than the baseline, while preserving image quality.

papers.title: Benchmarking LLM Inference on Desktop-Scale NVIDIA Grace Blackwell Clusters
papers.summary: Two NVIDIA DGX Spark GB10 systems connect directly over 200 GbE to serve larger language models and increase inference capacity, but the benefits depend on how they are deployed. We benchmark 17 open-weight checkpoints spanning dense and mixture-of-experts architectures, 8B to 235B parameters and four weight precisions on one and two RDMA-connected systems. Using vLLM, we compare tensor parallelism (TP=2), pipeline parallelism (PP=2) and a two-replica baseline at concurrency 1 to 64, with three independent launches per configuration. TP=2 delivers a median 1.59x peak-throughput gain over one Spark, versus 1.39x for PP=2 and has higher throughput in 93 of 96 matched comparisons with separated 95% Welch intervals. It reduces unloaded inter-token latency to 0.52x to 0.73x of one Spark, whereas PP=2 provides little reduction. TP=2 also achieves the highest goodput under a strict 100 ms inter-token latency objective wherever both strategies are supported and the objective is met. For models fitting on one Spark, TP=2 generally favors low-concurrency serving, while replication offers higher throughput at high concurrency. One Spark uses less GPU energy per output token at matched concurrency. Across three precision ladders, NVFP4 reduces unloaded latency more than adding a second Spark at BF16. NCCL microbenchmarks and comparisons with an earlier TCP campaign suggest that collective communication overhead contributes to the advantage of TP=2. These results provide deployment guidance for desktop-scale inference.

papers.title: Type-Confusion Security
papers.summary: Type systems are a lightweight way to obtain formal assurance that code upholds security properties. However, decentralized systems, such as smart contracts and Model Context Protocol ecosystems, have limited ability to constrain the behavior of untrusted code. In such systems, attackers may attempt to confuse trusted code by supplying values that do not behave according to their advertised types, an attack that we call type confusion. Well-known attacks such as confused deputy attacks, reentrancy attacks, and control-flow hijacking can be understood as instances of type confusion. We define type confusion security as the property that unrestricted attackers who need not follow the type system have no more power than limited attackers who fully obey it. We formally define type confusion security as a real--ideal emulation, and in the context of an information-flow-typed core calculus that statically enforces security against well-typed attackers, prove that its run-time checks also enforce security against ill-typed attackers. In this system, programmers can write code while reasoning about security only against well-typed attackers; the security guarantees enforced by the type system still hold. We mechanize a proof of type confusion security in Lean.

papers.title: Beyond Service Discovery: Coverage Awareness in LLM-Driven Service Composition
papers.summary: Large language models increasingly support the automated discovery and composition of services. In federated data ecosystems, this creates new opportunities for reusing existing data products and transformation services when constructing service-based data exchange modeled as data-sharing pipelines. However, finding relevant reusable assets does not imply that the available assets are sufficient to satisfy a consumer request. In this paper, we distinguish reuse discovery, the ability to identify relevant published assets, from reuse coverage, the extent to which the available assets support the transformations required by a request. We further consider coverage awareness, the ability of a composition system to recognize insufficient coverage. We investigate this distinction using PipeFinder, an LLM-driven framework for composing data-sharing pipelines, and evaluate 99 consumer requests against a fixed catalogue of data products and transformation services. Our experiments show that relevant data products can be discovered reliably, while successful composition remains considerably more difficult. More importantly, when required transformation services are missing, the framework typically constructs a pipeline from the available services rather than recognizing that the request cannot be satisfied. Explicitly incorporating coverage checking into the planning procedure substantially improves recognition of such cases. These results suggest that coverage awareness should be treated as an explicit concern in LLM-driven service composition and cannot be assumed to follow from improved discovery or model capability.

papers.title: Integrated GPU Core for Mamba-3
papers.summary: Mamba-3, the latest Mamba state-space model (SSM), enables efficient long-context modeling, matching Mamba-2 perplexity with half the state size and increasing decoding arithmetic intensity. However, its multi-input multi-output (MIMO) computation, exponential-trapezoidal discretization, and rotary positional embeddings (RoPE) introduce dense, element-wise, and sequential operations. Despite kernel fusion, conventional GPUs execute these operations inefficiently. Our characterization of Mamba-3 hybrid models reveals numerous kernel launches, substantial data movement, and increased register pressure that reduces warp occupancy and memory-latency hiding. We propose RescuCore, a specialized GPU execution unit for Mamba-3 inference that retains other hybrid model layers on existing GPU resources. Integrated alongside CUDA Cores and Tensor Cores within each Streaming Multiprocessor (SM) sub-partition, RescuCore shares the register file, shared memory, and warp schedulers. Dense projections remain on conventional GPU resources, while RescuCore pipelines discretization, normalization, RoPE, MIMO computation, recurrent state updates, and output gating to reduce kernel fragmentation and intermediate data movement. We select BF16 after evaluating multiple numerical formats, preserving model accuracy with an estimated area overhead of 5.9% of an A100 die for state size 32 and MIMO rank 4. We evaluate RescuCore using cycle-accurate Accel-Sim simulation, RTL synthesis, and synthesis-informed AccelWattch power modeling. Compared with conventional GPU execution, RescuCore achieves 1.4-9.4x speedup and 1.4-5.0x energy reduction during prefill, and 1.3-2.8x speedup and 1.2-2.6x energy reduction during autoregressive decoding. These results demonstrate the potential of GPU-integrated specialized execution for SSM-based hybrid models.

papers.title: Clock Distribution Network with Backside Clock Mesh in BSPDN Architecture
papers.summary: We propose a clock distribution network (CDN) in which the clock mesh is located on backside metal (BM) layers, while the rest of the network remains on the frontside. Since the backside power distribution network (BSPDN) also uses the BM layers, the clock mesh and power network must share them. We identify an important problem of placing mesh receivers while accounting for keep-out zones (KOZs) between clock- and power-nTSVs. We show that this problem can be solved using a potential-field method (PFM). Machine learning models are developed to place the mesh receivers: a U-Net predicts their initial positions, and an MLP predicts force weights for PFM-guided position refinement. Both models are trained through self-supervised learning by optimizing a differentiable objective that accounts for clock latency, IR-drop, and KOZ violations. Experimental results show that, on average, the proposed CDN reduces maximum local clock latency by 26%, global clock skew by 40%, and mesh switching power by 29% compared with a frontside CDN. On the same backside CDN, ML-guided PFM satisfies KOZ constraints while lowering IR-drop by 33% and requiring 85% fewer iterations than standard PFM.

papers.title: Strict Capabilities with a PNVI Escape Hatch
papers.summary: Capability systems enforce memory safety by tying pointers to their originating allocations, preventing forgery, use-after-free, and out-of-bounds accesses. Yet conventional capabilities are simultaneously too strict and not strict enough for C: they reject common low-level idioms involving integer casts or raw pointer bytes, while failing to enforce type correctness and sub-object bounds. Proposed Provenance Not Via Integers (PNVI) semantics expose this tension by permitting representation-level manipulation while retaining strict rules for ordinary pointer operations. We argue that these requirements call for two interoperable abstractions rather than a compromise within one. Strict capabilities enforce provenance, liveness, type correctness, and (sub-)object bounds; ordinary capability operations preserve these invariants. Exposed representations are non-dereferenceable, integer-like values that support arbitrary integer and byte-level manipulation under PNVI semantics while retaining unforgeability guarantees. They carry no directly usable memory-access authority: converting an exposed representation back to a strict capability reconstructs provenance under PNVI rules and validates type and bounds before access. Thus, low-level C idioms can use an explicit escape hatch without weakening ordinary capability derivation. We realize this design using Fully Randomized Pointers (FRP) and dynamic type metadata. Evaluation on low-level pointer idioms, Juliet tests, and existing C benchmarks shows that strict type and sub-object safety can coexist with low-level pointer manipulation.

papers.title: Partial Borrows in Rust
papers.summary: Rust ensures memory safety by requiring exclusive access to mutably borrowed data. However, a borrow can prevent access to more data than necessary. For example, a method with an &mut self parameter borrows the entire struct, even when the method uses only some of its fields. Calling the method can therefore conflict with an existing borrow of a field the method never uses, causing Rust to reject the program. Resolving such conflicts can require programmers to compromise useful abstractions, make non-local changes to their programs, or worse, resort to unsafe code. We introduce view types, a backward-compatible refinement of reference types that specifies which fields a reference may access. This allows methods to partially borrow a struct, accessing only the fields they need without blocking access to the rest. We establish the first fully mechanized foundation for Aeneas in Rocq. Along the way, we uncover and fix gaps in the original semantics and proofs. Building on this foundation, we formalize partial borrows and prove the extended borrow checking sound. We implement view types in rustc and extend the Aeneas interpreter to support partial borrows. Our evaluation shows how view types systematically resolve borrowing conflicts across method boundaries at no runtime cost.

papers.title: One Mean Can't Rule Them All
papers.summary: There has been extensive debate on how to summarize performance results, especially within the computer architecture community. This article presents a systematic approach to choosing the correct mean, aiming to answer this question for all computer scientists once and for all.

papers.title: Design Rules for Low-Latency Multipath Congestion Control
papers.summary: We first study optimal congestion control from a theoretical perspective. Concretely, we consider a system that optimizes the sum of the utilities of all the users, in which the users are allowed to send their traffic over different paths over the network and derive design rules that optimal (low-latency) multipath congestion control needs to follow. Because, as it turns out that optimal congestion control requires coordination between the network nodes, and hence, is hard to implement, we investigate how to approximate its performance with algorithms in which (i) the network nodes make independent decisions and (ii) coordination is only allowed between the subflows that belong to the same user. Therefore, these design rules need to be slightly relaxed. We compare the performance of these realistic algorithms with the optimal algorithm. We also investigate to what extent the algorithms that are currently defined and are being defined in the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF), in particular, (i) Prague congestion control (i.e., congestion control based on Accurate Explicit Congestion Notification (AccECN) marks) and (ii) a variant of a loss-based multipath congestion control algorithm, adhere to these rules.

papers.title: Building Fully On-Device GUI Agents with Mobile NPUs
papers.summary: Mobile GUI agents are increasingly used to automate everyday smartphone tasks, but most existing systems still rely on cloud-hosted models or remote inference, introducing repeated communication latency, privacy exposure, and dependence on network availability. Modern smartphones integrate neural processing units (NPUs) that provide an attractive substrate for fully on-device LLM inference. However, directly deploying conventional GUI-agent pipelines on mobile NPUs is inefficient. GUI-agent inference is fundamentally a long-input, short-output workload, yet conventional agents spend substantial time on autoregressive reasoning and action generation, while mobile NPUs provide much higher throughput for prompt prefill than token-by-token decoding. Meanwhile, dynamically varying GUI-agent contexts conflict with the fixed context profiles required by statically compiled NPU runtimes. We present DroidPrefill, a prefill-centric inference architecture that reshapes the GUI-agent workload around mobile-NPU execution. DroidPrefill combines Prefill-Centric Inference to reduce unnecessary autoregressive decoding with Efficient Context Management to preserve decision-critical information within a fixed compiled context budget. Experiments on commercial smartphones show that, in controlled comparisons with the autoregressive T3A+ baseline, DroidPrefill reduces per-step inference latency by up to 85.0%, while improving task success rate by up to 24.6%.

papers.title: Top-Level Operational Equilibrium: When is the response of a distributed system predictable from its own telemetry?
papers.summary: Distributed systems deployed across the edge-cloud continuum are adapted continuously: scaled, re-routed, given more or less capacity. Each adaptation rests on an expectation of how the system will respond, yet operators cannot tell from the telemetry they already collect whether that response is predictable. We define top-level operational equilibrium (TLOE), a notion of equilibrium for a running system, stated relative to the controls its operator declares. TLOE has three conditions: stationarity with time-scale separation, sufficiency of a top-level aggregate for the controls, and time-reversibility of that aggregate. We prove that an aggregate satisfying the last two exists if and only if the minimal sufficient statistic of the controls is time-reversible, so the coarsest admissible aggregate is derived rather than chosen. Under the first two conditions, the response to a small control change follows from passive telemetry through the steady-state fluctuation-response identity, with a conjugate observable fixed by the type of control: the total work in progress for a change of load, the occupancy of a stage for a change of its capacity. For chains of exponential single-server stages with Poisson input, TLOE holds exactly for load control at every stable throughput, but never for a control on the capacity of the first or last stage. On reference models, a per-stage conjugate overestimates the early response about threefold, blocking between stages breaks both conditions weakly, and a hysteretic autoscaler leaves no admissible aggregate at any reaction time computed. We specify a test for each condition, show that a static sufficiency test with an estimated top-level conjugate has no power, and quantify on simulated telemetry the window lengths the prediction and the reversibility test need. The evidence is on reference models; real telemetry is left to future work.

papers.title: Prediction-Driven Contract Matching with Controlled Overbooking for Cloud-Edge DDoS Scrubbing Markets
papers.summary: Cloud-edge distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) scrubbing requires ex-ante capacity commitments under uncertain traffic, heterogeneous budgets, resource costs, and fulfillment risks. We develop a prediction-driven two-stage contracting mechanism coordinating business entities (BEs), edge scrubbing nodes (ESs), and a cloud scrubbing center (CS) through BE-ES (B&E) main-service and ES-CS (E&C) supplementary contracts. In the first offline phase, Transformer forecasts generate candidate reserved scrubbing rates, generalized Nash bargaining determines candidate prices, and interim many-to-one B&E matching permits controlled overbooking under scenario-based aggregate ES shortfall-risk assessment. In the second offline phase, formal E&C reservations are established subject to capacity and payment constraints; their finalized rates and prices update ES-side proxy scores and guide localized risk-aware B&E contract adjustment. During online fulfillment, an edge-first, cloud-assisted weighted proportional allocation policy allocates scrubbing capacity under finalized contracts without rematching, renegotiation, or additional cloud reservations. Experiments with CICDDoS2019-derived workloads show that the proposed mechanism satisfies the prescribed empirical shortfall-risk criterion across all 100 evaluated horizon-instance pairs, whereas the NoRisk ablation violates it in all 100. Runtime measurements indicate lightweight online fulfillment relative to offline contract formation. The evaluated configurations also exhibit limited overall scrubbing coverage and near-zero realized cloud utilization.

papers.title: Investigating the Impact of CI-Source Sensitivity in Carbon-Aware Resource Management Systems
papers.summary: The sustainable growth of data centres increasingly depends on Resource-Management Systems (RMSs) that aim to reduce carbon emissions of computing workloads without degrading performance. This need is intensified by the rise of Artificial Intelligence (AI) workloads, which demand exponentially growing amounts of compute and energy across geographically distributed infrastructure. Recent carbon-aware RMSs exploit temporal and spatial variation in grid Carbon Intensity (CI) to shift workloads towards lower-carbon periods or locations. In practice, CI estimates and forecasts can be inaccurate and uncertain, and CI providers' methods differ substantially. Such discrepancies may have a significant impact on RMS placement decision-making, raising concerns about the fragility of existing solutions. Thus, in this work, we ask how discrepancies between plausible CI estimates propagate into resource-management decisions and operational outcomes. To answer this question, we harmonise and characterise CI traces from Wattnet and ElectricityMaps across five Central European zones. We then propose our evaluation framework: External CI Signal Characterisation And Perturbation Evaluation (ESCAPE), which assesses provider switching and controlled CI perturbations in a reproduced placement setting. We implement our framework using CarbonEdge as a use case, and measure changes in placement decisions and operational outcomes, such as carbon proxy, energy use, and latency. Our results show that switching CI-source changes the dominant placement site in 43.50% cases, and alters reported operational outcomes. These changes occur despite high rank correlation and structured disagreement between CI-sources. This observed sensitivity to CI-source choice motivates robustness-aware carbon-aware placement, in which CI uncertainty should be explicitly accounted for in resource-allocation decisions.

papers.title: Early UAV Detection Using 5G NR LEO Downlinks for Passive ISAC
papers.summary: 5G New Radio (NR) low-Earth-orbit (LEO) downlinks enable passive integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) detection. Weak echoes require motion-compensated accumulation, but exhaustive searches postpone alerts. We propose a receiver that combines selective Doppler-rate search, early UAV alerts and continued delay-Doppler estimation. Classical, statistical and neural configurations select rates of Doppler change to search, while a shared correlation score determines detection. Simulated echo delay, Doppler and power follow the moving satellite-UAV-receiver geometry, propagation loss, assumed scattering and antenna response. In a line-of-sight scene with acquired beams and UAVs at 5-8 km horizontal distance, all three configurations match exhaustive search at 92.9% correct final detections, with 0.10-0.13% observed false alerts on no-UAV recordings. The neural configuration reduces mean time to the first correct alert by 36.5% versus exhaustive search and 21.9% versus the closest literature baseline, averaging over successfully detected UAVs. These results demonstrate earlier UAV alerts while preserving exhaustive search's final detection accuracy, supporting passive sensing over cellular satellites.

papers.title: CIRT: Calculus of Inductive Refinement Types
papers.summary: Refinement types are a powerful mechanism for statically verifying properties of programs. They have been successfully integrated into practical languages such as Haskell, Scala, and Rust. However, their metatheory is not yet fully understood. In this paper we present the first semantic model for a refinement type system that supports the full feature combination of subtyping, SMT-style equality, impredicative polymorphism, and (stratified) inductive types. Interactions between these features have led to inconsistencies in the past, and existing formalizations of refinement type systems omit at least one of them. We present a realizability model based on partial equivalence relations (PERs) over a Scott domain, which overcomes these obstacles. We use our model to prove the consistency of a core refinement type system and to give a semantic account of the annotation-independence property of refinement types. Our semantics uses two interpretations: a refined one, which interprets types and their refinements as PERs; and an unrefined one, consisting of complete uniform PERs with a bottom element (CUPERs), which models computational behaviour independently of refinements. We extend the model to positive and stratified inductive types, showing that both are consistent in the presence of impredicativity.

papers.title: Disaggregated LLM Inference in Space: A Communication Feasibility Study
papers.summary: Orbital data centers could enable large-scale AI inference, but efficiently serving a frontier language model to many users may require several compute satellites to cooperate over optical links. While disaggregated inference, which splits large language model (LLM) serving across machines, is well established in terrestrial data centers, its viability under the unique constraints of orbital deployments remains an open question. This article investigates how link capacity and satellite separation affect two types of disaggregated LLM serving, in both compact satellite formations and distributed constellations. Prefill-decode disaggregation (PDD) migrates a large KV cache once per request, while attention-FFN disaggregation (AFD) exchanges small activations at every mixture-of-experts layer for every generated token. The two respond to distance in different ways. PDD is limited mainly by link capacity and, with fast enough links, tolerates separations of up to a thousand kilometers. AFD is limited mainly by propagation delay, which accumulates layer by layer and forces attention and expert instances within about a kilometer of each other. Based on these results, we propose a hierarchical orbital inference architecture and provide network design guidelines for future orbital data centers, including the role of ground access latency.

papers.title: From Strong Normalization to WhatsApp: the Journey of an Axiom
papers.summary: Twenty years ago, Mariangiola Dezani-Ciancaglini, Daniele Varacca and I showed that Milner's classic encoding of functions into processes does not respect one of the laws of intersection types, the one stating that $(\sigma\to\tau)\land(\sigma\to\rho)$ is a subtype of $\sigma\to(\tau\land\rho)$, which Barendregt, Coppo and Dezani-Ciancaglini had stated in 1983 for their filter $\lambda$-model. In this essay I show that this observation is the key to closing what a colleague at Meta calls ``the main typing gap in Erlang''---the language in which the servers of WhatsApp are written: the type of the function that implements a server is not related to the type of the server, so that a client may expect from the server a reply that the server will never send. Actually, closing this gap is just an excuse to follow the journey of the law above, and of some of its relatives, from the study of strong normalization in the $\lambda$-calculus to the type systems of Elixir and Erlang: a journey that shows how much the practical typing of these languages owes to the work of Mario Coppo, Mariangiola Dezani-Ciancaglini and Simona Ronchi Della Rocca, to whom this essay is dedicated for their eightieth birthdays.

papers.title: Underpinning Property-Based Testing
papers.summary: As the property-based testing community strives to automate challenging parts of the process away from users --- in particular, the construction of generators --- it is critical that we can clearly state what it means for that automation to be correct. We present a new framework for PBT, implemented in the Lean theorem prover, that provides a more solid foundation to build on. Our generators are interpretable: interpreted one way, they can be run efficiently as programs that sample randomness; and interpreted another way, they enable a wide range of correctness proofs, including proofs about distributions that other foundational PBT models do not support. We evaluate our framework extensively, with both small and large benchmarks and case studies, arguing that the extra power brought by distributional proofs is practically important for the next generation of generator automation.

papers.title: CompCert4Lean: Porting a Verified C Compiler to Lean in Six Weeks with Parallel Coding Agents
papers.summary: We present CompCert4Lean, a large-scale port of CompCert 3.17's verified compiler core from Rocq to Lean, completed in approximately six weeks by one expert directing parallel LLM agents. Our migration workflow partitions the development along its dependencies, audits translated definitions and theorem statements before large-scale proof reconstruction, and then reconstructs proofs in parallel against stable interfaces. The resulting compiler covers typed CompCert C through x86-64 assembly, discharges all 4,908 recorded proof obligations without project-specific axioms, and produces executable Linux binaries. The workflow enabled the expert to concentrate on organizing the work rather than supplying technical solutions. Of 1,071 human interactions, 88.8% concerned workflow and coordination, while only three supplied technical direction. Optimization campaigns further demonstrate the benefit of the Lean port for agent-driven verified development. Under matched budgets of 24 active hours, GPT-6-astra produced a Lean candidate with 11.7% lower generated-program runtime across 29 small-tests programs, compared with 2.3% lower for its Rocq candidate, both relative to original CompCert 3.17 and while preserving the end-to-end correctness theorem. These results show that parallel LLM agents can support large-scale migration with limited human technical direction and subsequently improve the migrated compiler while retaining its formal guarantees.

papers.title: SAFE: Formal Specification and Implementation of a Scalable Analysis Framework for ECMAScript
papers.summary: The prevalent uses of JavaScript in web programming have revealed security vulnerability issues of JavaScript applications, which emphasizes the need for JavaScript analyzers to detect such issues. Recently, researchers have proposed several analyzers of JavaScript programs and some web service companies have developed various JavaScript engines. However, unfortunately, most of the tools are not documented well, thus it is very hard to understand and modify them. Or, such tools are often not open to the public. In this paper, we present formal specification and implementation of SAFE, a scalable analysis framework for ECMAScript, developed for the JavaScript research community. This is the very first attempt to provide both formal specification and its opensource implementation for JavaScript, compared to the existing approaches focused on only one of them. To make it more amenable for other researchers to use our framework, we formally define three kinds of intermediate representations for JavaScript used in the framework, and we provide formal specifications of translations between them. To be adaptable for adventurous future research including modifications in the original JavaScript syntax, we actively use open-source tools to automatically generate parsers and some intermediate representations. To support a variety of program analyses in various compilation phases, we design the framework to be as flexible, scalable, and pluggable as possible. Finally, our framework is publicly available, and some collaborative research using the framework are in progress.

papers.title: A Matter of Stages: Energy-Latency Trade-offs in Multimodal LLM Serving
papers.summary: Online serving of multimodal large language models requires deciding whether to separate visual encoding (E), prefill (P), and decode (D) across GPUs and how to configure their frequencies. EPD disaggregation enables independent stage control, but it also changes communication and queueing behavior. Lowering one stage's frequency can increase queueing and prolong execution across the EPD pipeline. Consequently, reducing power at one stage does not necessarily reduce total GPU energy per request. In this paper, we systematically characterize fused and EPD-disaggregated serving across four multimodal models under a fixed three-GPU budget, followed by single-stage and uniform downclocking experiments across 18 workload combinations.
